Topology Views Dashboard — Complete User Guide

This guide provides a comprehensive explanation of the Topology Views Dashboard, which visualizes infrastructure topology data stored in GraphDB. The dashboard provides three complementary views through the following tabs:

The example below walks through the Full Stack tab for the PETCLINIC application together with its Application Component (petclinic-web01), the severity legend, status filters, Timeline button, and search functionality.

1. Dashboard Overview

The Topology Views Dashboard answers three complementary questions about the same GraphDB topology:

  • Full Stack — "What does the vertical stack look like for this asset?" (layers such as App → Application Component → Network → Storage → Compute → Virtualization → Wireless).
  • Asset Map — "How is this asset connected in the graph?" (interactive nodes, edges, grouping, pan/zoom).
  • Relationships — "Who are the direct and typed neighbors?" (inbound/outbound tables grouped by node type).

All three widgets read from the same GraphDB topology and refresh together whenever you select a node from the left navigation panel.

2. Left Navigation Panel

The left navigation panel provides a two-column browser for selecting assets:

PETCLINIC
Online Banking Application
  • First Column (tree_data): Groups nodes by type or application name (e.g., PETCLINIC, Online Banking Application)
  • Second Column (tree_detail): Lists individual nodes with Node ID and Node Name
  • Search Box: Find nodes by name
  • Node Icons: Visual type indicators (enabled with showNodeIcon: true)
  • Auto-Select: First item auto-selected on load (enabled with autoSelectFirstItem: true)
Note: In the example above, PETCLINIC is highlighted in blue (active selection), while Online Banking Application appears in grey (inactive). This indicates the user has selected the PETCLINIC application to view its topology.

4. Full Stack Tab (Default Active Tab)

The Full Stack tab shows a layer-ordered stack diagram centered on the currently selected node. It is best for understanding vertical dependencies. Alert severity is displayed directly on stack elements, giving you an at-a-glance health view across the full infrastructure chain.

4.1 Severity Legend

At the top of the Full Stack view, a color-coded severity legend helps you quickly identify alert levels:

4.2 Status Filters

Below the severity legend, status filters allow you to control which alerts are visible:

Status:
  • Active (checked): Shows nodes with currently active alerts
  • Cleared (checked): Shows nodes with recently cleared alerts
  • Hide nodes without alerts (toggle off): When enabled, hides nodes that have no alerts, focusing only on problematic nodes
In this example: Both Active and Cleared checkboxes are checked (blue), meaning both active and cleared alerts are shown. The Hide nodes without alerts toggle is OFF (grey), so all nodes are visible regardless of alert status.

4.3 Toolbar Controls

On the right side of the filter bar, two important controls are available:

  • Timeline Button: Opens a timeline view to track changes and alert history over time for the selected topology
  • Search nodes...: A search box to quickly find specific nodes within the stack by name

Use Full Stack when you want to understand the vertical layer structure of an asset and see alert counts integrated into the stack.

Don't use Full Stack when you need a free-form graph layout (use Asset Map) or a precise typed neighbor list (use Relationships).

5. Asset Map Tab

The Asset Map tab displays a free-form interactive graph of your infrastructure. Nodes represent assets, edges represent connections, and similar nodes are auto-grouped to keep large topologies manageable. Alert severity decorates nodes with color-coded badges.

Key Features:

  • Interactive Graph: Pan, zoom, and navigate the topology freely
  • Auto-Grouping: Similar nodes are automatically grouped to reduce visual clutter
  • Alert Overlays: Color-coded alert badges on nodes matching the severity legend
  • Nodes Panel: Searchable table listing all nodes with details (Name, Layer, Node Type, vCenter, Data Center)
  • Edges Panel: Table showing all connections with source, destination, and relation type
  • Toolbar: Zoom controls, layout options, and view toggles

Use Asset Map when you want to explore overall connectivity, identify clusters of related assets, or navigate freely through the graph.

Don't use Asset Map when you need a precise typed relationship list (use Relationships).

6. Relationships Tab

The Relationships tab shows the inbound and outbound connections of the selected node in a structured tabular format, grouped by connection direction and neighbor node type.

Key Features:

  • Typed Connections: Clear separation of inbound vs outbound relationships
  • Grouped View: Organized by neighbor type (e.g., "Connected to 1 Webserver(s)")
  • Node Details: Node Type, Node ID, and Node Label for each connection
  • Context Actions: Click to open Asset Stack View for any neighbor
  • Expand/Collapse: Toggle visibility of connection groups

Use Relationships when you want a precise neighbor list, need to audit dependencies, or troubleshoot typed connectivity.

Don't use Relationships when you need a visual graph layout (use Asset Map) or full node attribute details (use Full Stack).

7. End-to-End Workflow

  1. Open the Topology Views Dashboard.
  2. In the left navigator, expand an application or node type (e.g., PETCLINIC, as shown in the example above).
  3. Select a node from the detail list — all three tabs refresh automatically.
  4. Use Full Stack to understand vertical layer context and alert status (as shown in the example above).
  5. Use Asset Map to explore neighbors, expand auto-groups, and inspect edges.
  6. Use Relationships for a precise inbound/outbound inventory.
  7. Click Asset Stack View from any tab to drill into a focused view for that asset.

8. Alert Integration

9. Tips & Tricks

Pro Tips:
  • Use the Search nodes... box (visible in the toolbar above) to quickly find nodes by name within the stack.
  • Use the Timeline button to track alert history and topology changes over time.
  • Toggle Hide nodes without alerts ON to focus only on problematic nodes during incident response.
  • In Asset Map, use the Nodes panel to filter and search for specific assets in the graph.
  • Enable auto-grouping for better performance on large topologies.
  • Click expand/collapse icons in Relationships to show/hide connection groups.
  • Adjust the time filter if nodes don't appear — they may be outside the selected window.
Common Pitfalls:
  • Navigator tree empty: Check the time filter — node timestamps may be outside the selected window.
  • No connections on Asset Map: Verify the node has edges registered in GraphDB.
  • Relationships tab empty: Check the relation map configuration for the selected node type.
  • Alerts not showing: Ensure the alert stream node ID matches the topology node ID.
  • Drill-down app blank: The Asset Stack View action requires node_id and stack definition in context.
  • Stale data: Click refresh if data seems outdated.

11. JSON Dashboard Definition Overview

The Topology Views Documentation dashboard is configured as a dashboard type with the following key sections:

  • dashboard_filters — Time filter disabled for static documentation
  • dashboard_sections[] — Contains a single "Documentation" section with:
    • A label widget (widget_type: "label") containing the full HTML documentation
    • Comprehensive explanations of all three tabs, filters, legends, and workflows
